newsitem.title: GERMANY: German firms not ready for millennium bug - study.
newsitem.headline: German firms not ready for millennium bug - study.

text.p: A majority of companies polled by a leading German insurance company said they were not prepared for the "Millennium bug" that threatens to bring the world's computers to a halt at the turn of the century.

German reinsurer Cologne Re said 60 percent of the 124 companies polled from the chemical, engineering and banking sectors said they had not yet fully analysed their computer systems, while 31 percent said they had done nothing at all.

Alexander Quack-Grobecker, the Cologne Re executive in charge of the study, said he did not expect a "meltdown" as often prophesied in the computer industry, but at the same time said it was too early to give the all-clear.

Because computers have been programmed to recognise only the last two digits in the year, when the date changes to 2000 they will record this as 1900, unleashing potential chaos on financial markets and in businesses around the globe.
The issue is of concern to insurance firms who fear damage claims from companies should computers systems collapse and hit services, causing loss of revenue and perhaps other problems.
Cologne Re said the potential damage claims at the companies polled could reach as high as 900 million marks.
Chemical giant Bayer AG said it could face damages of up to six million marks from 30-year-old computer programmes that could fail at the turn of the millennium.
Industry experts have estimated that world-wide the damages could be as high as $300 billion.
